title: Filtered colimits of quasi-coherent algebras; sections over affines
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a directed set and $(\mathcal A_i,\varphi_{i'i})$ ($i\le i'$) a directed system of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras (sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras, quasi-coherent as $\mathcal O_S$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]). Then the colimit $\mathcal A=\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i$ exists in the category of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] (it is the sheafification of the presheaf colimit $U\mapsto\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)$, and also the colimit in all sheaves of $\mathcal O_S$-algebras), and for every affine open $U\subseteq S$ the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)\to\mathcal A(U)$ is an isomorphism of rings. Moreover the formation of $\mathcal A$ commutes with restriction to an open $V\subseteq S$: $\mathcal A|_V=\varinjlim_i(\mathcal A_i|_V)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent, line 1435; colimits of quasi-coherent sheaves on Spec R are M~ with M the colimit of the modules) and Section 26.24 (section-quasi-coherent, line 4717, item (4): any colimit of quasi-coherent sheaves is quasi-coherent); used in Limits, Lemma 01YX ('This is a quasi-coherent sheaf of O_{S_0}-algebras, see Schemes, Section 26.24')

proof.text: *Step 1 (the colimit in sheaves of $\mathcal O_S$-algebras).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebras-directed-colimit] to the topological space $S$ with its structure sheaf $\mathcal O_S$ and the system $(\mathcal A_i,\varphi_{i'i})$: the presheaf $\mathcal P:U\mapsto\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)$ is a presheaf of commutative rings under $\mathcal O_S$, its sheafification $\theta:\mathcal P\to\mathcal A=\mathcal P^\#$ as a presheaf of commutative rings is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras, and with $\iota_i=\theta\circ c_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal A$ the pair $(\mathcal A,(\iota_i))$ is (1) a colimit of the system in the category of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras and (2), forgetting the multiplications, a colimit of the underlying $\mathcal O_S$-modules in $\Mod(\mathcal O_S)$. This gives the existence of $\mathcal A$, its description as the sheafification of the presheaf colimit, and its universal property among all sheaves of $\mathcal O_S$-algebras.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 009E item (3) and Lemma 0087; Modules, Lemma 01AH (2)

proof.text: *Step 2 (restriction to an open).* Let $V\subseteq S$ be open, with inclusion $j:V\to S$ (an open immersion). For a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras $\mathcal B$ the restriction $\mathcal B|_V$ ($W\mapsto\mathcal B(W)$ for $W\subseteq V$) is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_V$-algebras whose underlying $\mathcal O_V$-module is the restriction of the underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module of [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and restriction of morphisms is a functor. The restricted maps $\iota_i|_V:\mathcal A_i|_V\to\mathcal A|_V$ form a cocone of $\mathcal O_V$-algebras on $(\mathcal A_i|_V)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebras-directed-colimit] applied on $V$ there is a colimit $(\mathcal B,(\beta_i))$ of $(\mathcal A_i|_V)$ in sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_V$-algebras whose underlying module is a colimit in $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$, and a unique algebra map $u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A|_V$ with $u\beta_i=\iota_i|_V$. By Step 1(2), $(\mathcal A,(\iota_i))$ is a colimit of $\mathcal O_S$-modules, so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](1) $(\mathcal A|_V,(\iota_i|_V))$ is a colimit of the $\mathcal A_i|_V$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_V)$; hence $u$, being the comparison map between two colimits of the same diagram of $\mathcal O_V$-modules, is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_V$-modules, i.e. bijective on every $W\subseteq V$. A bijective ring homomorphism has a ring-homomorphism inverse, so $u$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_V$-algebras: $\mathcal A|_V=\varinjlim_i(\mathcal A_i|_V)$ with the coprojections $\iota_i|_V$, both in sheaves of $\mathcal O_V$-algebras and (Step 5) in quasi-coherent ones.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AJ (2) (pullback, here restriction to an open, commutes with colimits); Sheaves, Lemma 00A0

proof.text: *Step 3 (an affine open: $\mathcal A$ is $\widetilde M$).* Let $U\subseteq S$ be an affine open and $R=\mathcal O_S(U)$. Since $U$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)=R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], there is an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\cong U$ inducing the identity on global sections; composing with the inclusion gives an open immersion $g:X=\operatorname{Spec}R\to S$ with image $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits] (with $f=g$) the modules $\mathcal A_i|_X$ are quasi-coherent ((2), as the $\mathcal A_i$ are), $\Gamma(X,\mathcal A_i|_X)=\mathcal A_i(U)=:M_i$ and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal A|_X)=\mathcal A(U)$ as $R$-modules, and by (1) together with Step 1(2) $(\mathcal A|_X,(\iota_i|_X))$ is a colimit of $(\mathcal A_i|_X)$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) the counits $\varepsilon_i:\widetilde{M_i}\to\mathcal A_i|_X$ are isomorphisms, and they are natural: $(\varphi_{i'i}|_X)\circ\varepsilon_i=\varepsilon_{i'}\circ\widetilde{\varphi_{i'i,U}}$. So the diagram $(\widetilde{M_i},\widetilde{\varphi_{i'i,U}})$ is isomorphic to $(\mathcal A_i|_X)$. Let $(M,(c_i))$ be the colimit of the $R$-modules $M_i$ along the $\varphi_{i'i,U}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4) $(\widetilde M,(\widetilde{c_i}))$ is a colimit of $(\widetilde{M_i})$, hence there is a unique isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\psi:\widetilde M\to\mathcal A|_X$ with $\psi\circ\widetilde{c_i}=\iota_i|_X\circ\varepsilon_i$ for all $i$ (uniqueness of colimits up to unique isomorphism, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]).

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent: on Spec R the colimit of the M_i~ is (colim M_i)~), via Lemma 01I7 (mapping property) and Lemma 01IA/01IB

proof.text: *Step 4 (sections over the affine open).* Take global sections in Step 3. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2) and the triangle identity of the adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1) ($\Gamma(\varepsilon_{\mathcal F})\circ\tau_X=\mathrm{id}_{\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)}$ for $\mathcal F=\mathcal A_i|_X$), the $R$-linear bijection $\lambda=\Gamma(X,\psi)\circ\tau_X:M\to\mathcal A(U)$ satisfies $\lambda(c_i(m))=\iota_{i,U}(m)$ for $m\in M_i=\mathcal A_i(U)$. Let $C=\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)$ be the directed colimit of commutative rings with coprojections $d_i$, and $\kappa:C\to\mathcal A(U)$ the canonical ring map, $\kappa d_i=\iota_{i,U}$. The maps $d_i$ are additive and $R$-linear ($R$ acting through $\mathcal O_S(U)\to\mathcal A_i(U)$), so there is a unique $R$-linear $\mu:M\to C$ with $\mu c_i=d_i$, and $\kappa\mu=\lambda$ (both send $c_i(m)$ to $\iota_{i,U}(m)$). By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise](2) (with the base ring $\mathbf Z$: commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebras are commutative rings) every element of $C$ is some $d_i(a)=\mu(c_i(a))$, so $\mu$ is surjective; since $\kappa\mu=\lambda$ is injective, $\mu$ is injective too. Hence $\mu$ is bijective and $\kappa=\lambda\mu^{-1}$ is a bijective ring homomorphism, i.e. the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)\to\mathcal A(U)$ is an isomorphism of rings.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HV (2) (Γ(Spec R, M~) = M) and Lemma 01ID

proof.text: *Step 5 (quasi-coherence; the colimit among quasi-coherent algebras).* Every point of $S$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U$ [def-pc-scheme], and by Step 3, transported along $\operatorname{Spec}R\cong U$, $\mathcal A|_U\cong\widetilde M$ with $\widetilde M$ quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; so the underlying $\mathcal O_S$-module of $\mathcal A$ is quasi-coherent by the definition [pqf-def-coherent] (local of the form $\widetilde M$ on affine neighbourhoods). Quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras form a full subcategory of sheaves of commutative $\mathcal O_S$-algebras containing all $\mathcal A_i$ and $\mathcal A$, so the colimit of Step 1 is also the colimit in quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The same applies on any open $V$ to the colimit of Step 2 (the $\mathcal A_i|_V$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2)).

split_report.summary: Split into five steps. The algebra part (existence, sheafification of the presheaf colimit, universal property among sheaves of O_S-algebras, underlying module = colimit in Mod(O_S)) is the new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-algebras-directed-colimit (Sheaves 009E(3), 0087, Modules 01AH; no sheaf-of-algebras notion in Mathlib). Restriction to opens: new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits (Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor ⊣ pushforward, isQuasicoherent_restrictFunctor), plus the elementary fact that a bijective algebra map is an isomorphism. Affine opens: new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction (tilde.adjunction, unit iso, isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent, left adjoints preserve colimits) gives A|_U ≅ (colim M_i)~ (Schemes 01ID via 01I7) and sections = colim M_i; the comparison with the ring colimit uses the reviewed leaf lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise (2). Quasi-coherence and the colimit among quasi-coherent algebras are elementary (definition pqf-def-coherent; full subcategory). Sheaves 009F/Sites 0738 (sections of directed colimits over qc opens) is not needed: the affine sections come from M~. Stmt deps def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category and def-weil-pbc-sheafification added (the statement uses O_S-modules and sheafification).
